result:
All 617 tests pass. The fix is complete.

Root cause: in `src/lib/event-bus.ts`, `subscribe()`'s returned unsubscribe closure captured a private snapshot `Set` taken at subscribe time, then deleted from that snapshot. Every subsequent `subscribe()` call for the same event type replaced the map's entry with a new copied set, orphaning earlier snapshots. Since multiple services (activity, usage, webhook) all subscribe to the same event types during `registerEventHandlers()`, only the last-subscribed handler's unsubscribe closure still pointed at the live set — the earlier ones silently no-op'd on detach, leaking handlers that then doubled up on the next `registerEventHandlers()` call. In-app notifications were unaffected because `notification-service.ts` self-registers once at module import, entirely outside the detach/reattach cycle.

Fixed by having the unsubscribe closure always read the *current* live set from the map at call time (copy-on-write on delete too), so detaching removes exactly that handler regardless of how many other subscriptions happened afterward for the same type.
